source_text: Ἔσχατοι καιροί. λοιπὸν αἰσχυνθῶμεν, φοβηθῶμεν τὴν μακροθυμίαν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα μὴ ἡμῖν εἰς κρίμα γένηται. ἦ γὰρ τὴν μέλλουσαν ὀργὴν φοβηθῶμεν, ἦ τὴν ἐνεστῶσαν χάριν ἀγαπήσωμεν, ἒν τῶν δύο: μόνον ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ εὑρεθῆναι εἰς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ζῆν.
thought_title: Last times: fear God's patience or love his grace
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Ephesus, urging them to live in a way worthy of the last times, either fearing God's coming wrath or loving his present grace, so as to be found in Christ Jesus for true life.
pass_a_gloss: Last times. Henceforth let us be ashamed, let us fear the patience of God, in order that it may not become for us into judgment. For either let us fear the coming wrath, or let us love the present grace, one of the two: only to be found in Christ Jesus for the true life.

choices.why: Keeps the abrupt, prophetic tone of the Greek nominative phrase without adding a copula, matching Ignatius's urgent style.
The aorist passive subjunctive expresses a call to a decisive change of attitude, not a continuous state; 'be ashamed' captures the passive force.
The genitive is objective—God's patience toward sinners—and 'patience' preserves the compound sense of long-suffering without archaism.
The perfect participle ἐνεστῶσαν means 'standing in, present,' and contrasts with the future wrath; 'present' keeps the temporal opposition sharp.
The neuter singular ἒν with the partitive genitive is a stark either/or; the literal rendering preserves the disjunctive force.
The articular infinitive with εἰς expresses purpose or result; 'for the true life' keeps the goal-oriented sense without over-translating.

pass_b_english: These are the last times. From now on let us be ashamed, and let us fear the patience of God, so that it may not become judgment for us. Either let us fear the wrath that is coming, or let us love the grace that is present—one of the two. Only let us be found in Christ Jesus for the true life.

last_rejected.why: αἰσχυνθῶμεν means 'let us be ashamed' but context demands 'let us feel shame/reverence'; 'ashamed' suggests embarrassment not moral compunction.
last_rejected.ruling: αἰσχυνθῶμεν means 'be ashamed'; moral compunction is within its range. Not a major error.

last_rejected.why: μακροθυμία is 'longsuffering/forbearance' not 'patience' in modern sense; God's withholding judgment, not calm waiting.
last_rejected.ruling: 'patience' is a standard gloss for μακροθυμία; 'longsuffering' is a preference, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: so that it may not become judgment for us
last_rejected.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ ἡμῖν εἰς κρίμα γένηται
last_rejected.why: Subject of γένηται is God's forbearance, not 'it' vaguely; 'become judgment' obscures that his patience turns to judgment.
last_rejected.fix: lest his forbearance become judgment upon us
last_rejected.ruling: 'it' naturally refers to God's patience; 'become judgment' preserves εἰς κρίμα γένηται adequately.
